data.name: Chaperone-mediated autophagy
data.description: A selective form of autophagy in which a cytosolic chaperone delivers single proteins to the lysosomal surface, where they unfold and are pulled in through a LAMP2A translocation complex. No vesicle is formed, which is what distinguishes it from macroautophagy. Regulated at the lysosome by an mTORC2/PHLPP1/Akt axis (ARI2015), so mTOR's relationship to autophagy here runs through a different complex than the canonical mTORC1-ULK1 step.
data.description_beginner: A tidier kind of recycling: instead of wrapping a whole chunk of the cell in a bag, a helper protein carries one damaged protein at a time to the lysosome and threads it through a gate in the wall.
